chapter: Building the band: Dave Duncan, Denver and Rene Hall
title: Walter Pichon, the arranger who forgot to book gigs
summary: Rene tells of Walter Pichon in New Orleans, so absorbed in music that he lined up no work after a Memphis hotel engagement; Fields still has his arrangement of Stardust.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: You see, I was booking the band a lot too and he says I know, and I don't want you to give up what you're doing, because you're getting work for us, and he said one reason that I like you is--he said one of the reasons I made up my mind to come with you is I was playing with Walter Pichon, a very fine musician and arranger, but he was too enthused over music. He said, we would have a rehearsal and if a man came up to talk to him about a gig, he would say just a minute. He wouldn't be insulting, but his mind would be on that music; that man might stand there for a half hour to forty five minutes, and he'd get tired and go about his business. And so we had to tell him, that man wanted to give us a gig; oh man, I forgot about that, I was trying to get this arrangement.

And so finally, one time they got a--he saw that the guys were getting kind of tired with the way things were going, they would get a good job and not know when there was another one, so they got a job in some hotel,

in Memphis, a white band, a big white hotel in Memphis, and said Pichon gave one of those little pep talks, he said we got two weeks in there, we'll be in one place for two weeks and we'll have some work, we'll have plenty of work, because I'll be in one place and I can call and get everything lined up.

So they went in there and everything went down just fine and Pichon was so enthused over them going over good and he just forgot about everything and a day or two before it was over, somebody said, Pichon, where do we go from here? I've been so busy, you've all been doing such a good job, I just wanted to keep you on your feet, but we're going back home and we'll get something.
He didn't have nothing in the world.
Do you remember how to spell it?

No, but I think I have a picture that he gave me. He's passed now but he was a very fine arranger and we had that arrangement and Rene had him send an arrangement to me after then and we had one that as time changed that never did get old and after Ernie got up big--yeah, my son--he said, dad, there's one thing that I would like to have and that's the arrangement of Stardust that you all used to do, and I lost my whole repetoire. But Pichon was a very fine arranger.
